external_entities.name: colleagues
external_entities.description: People who sign in through the identity broker and use applications.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.
external_entities.notes: The text does not specify whether colleagues are asked for a second factor.

external_entities.name: franchise colleagues
external_entities.description: Colleagues from franchise stores who authenticate through their own identity provider.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in.
external_entities.notes: The text does not specify which colleagues the franchise identity provider is allowed to vouch for.

external_entities.name: HR system
external_entities.description: System supplying colleague group-membership changes to the identity broker overnight.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Group membership is not maintained there by hand — it comes from the HR system overnight.

external_entities.name: identity provider
external_entities.description: The identity provider used by franchise colleagues to vouch for them.
external_entities.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them
external_entities.notes: The text does not specify which colleagues this provider is allowed to vouch for.

processes.name: identity broker
processes.description: Signs colleagues in, issues tokens, validates federated sign-ins, pulls group changes, and writes sign-ins to an audit log.
processes.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker. The broker runs on the corporate network.
processes.notes: The broker takes franchise identity-provider vouching as a sign-in. Tokens are valid for twelve hours and cannot be pulled back before expiry.

processes.name: store admin console
processes.description: Application that uses token groups to authorize price changes and transaction voids across stores.
processes.source_excerpt: The store admin console is one of those applications. It also runs on the corporate network.
processes.notes: A store-manager token works against every store because the console does not check which store the colleague belongs to.

data_stores.name: key store
data_stores.description: Store holding the signing key used by the identity broker for tokens.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.
data_stores.notes: The text does not specify whether the key store is encrypted where it sits.

data_stores.name: directory
data_stores.description: The identity broker's directory of colleagues and their group memberships.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.
data_stores.notes: The text does not specify whether the directory is encrypted where it sits.

data_stores.name: audit log
data_stores.description: Log to which the broker writes sign-ins.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down what the log records or whether it covers the franchise route. The text does not specify whether the log is encrypted where it sits.

data_flows.name: sign-in
data_flows.description: Colleagues sign in to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.
data_flows.data_description: Colleague sign-in credentials and identity information

data_flows.name: issue token
data_flows.description: The identity broker issues a token to a signed-in colleague.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Once the broker has signed a colleague in it issues them a token. The token carries the colleague's staff id and a list of the groups they are in.
data_flows.data_description: Token carrying the colleague's staff id and group membership

data_flows.name: federated sign-in
data_flows.description: Franchise colleagues use their own identity provider's vouching as a sign-in to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in.

data_flows.name: vouch for colleague
data_flows.description: The franchise identity provider vouches for a franchise colleague to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them
data_flows.notes: The text does not specify which colleagues the provider is allowed to vouch for.

data_flows.name: use console
data_flows.description: A colleague presents a token to the store admin console to change prices or void transactions.
data_flows.source_excerpt: If the token has the store-manager group in it, the console lets the holder change prices and void transactions.
data_flows.notes: The console decides what the colleague may do from token groups and does not check which store the colleague belongs to.
data_flows.data_description: Token carrying staff id and groups, plus price-change or transaction-void commands

data_flows.name: fetch public key
data_flows.description: The store admin console fetches the broker's public signing key.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Applications fetch the public half from the broker to check the signature.
data_flows.data_description: Public half of the token-signing key

data_flows.name: sync membership
data_flows.description: The HR system supplies colleague group-membership changes to the identity broker overnight.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker pulls the changes once a night
data_flows.notes: The text says this is also how leavers stop being colleagues.

data_flows.name: update directory
data_flows.description: The identity broker maintains its directory of colleagues and groups.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.

data_flows.name: read signing key
data_flows.description: The identity broker reads the signing key it uses to sign tokens.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_flows.name: write sign-ins
data_flows.description: The identity broker writes sign-in events to the audit log.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_flows.notes: The text does not specify what the log records or whether it covers the franchise route.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network on which the identity broker and store admin console run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The broker runs on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: home devices
trust_boundaries.description: Colleagues' own devices at home from which they may sign in.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: including their own devices at home

assumptions.assumption: The directory contains personal information because it stores colleagues and their staff-related group memberships.
assumptions.basis: The text says the directory keeps colleagues and the groups they are in.

assumptions.assumption: The key store contains confidential information because it stores a token-signing key.
assumptions.basis: The text says the broker keeps a signing key in the key store.
